sentences.text: Wanosuchus is an extinct genus of sebecosuchian mesoeucrocodylian.
The only known specimen of Wanosuchus is a nearly complete lower jaw.
This lower jaw lacks an external mandibular fenestra, a hole in the bone, and contains thirteen teeth.
The fourth and eleventh teeth are the longest in the jaw.
The species name atresus refers to the missing external mandibular fenestra, a unique trait for this animal.
Wanosuchus shares some characteristics with the Late Cretaceous crocodyliform Doratodon.
The fossil was collected between 1970 and 1972 by personnel from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.
Wanosuchus was named in 1981 by Zhang Fakui.
Zhang classified Wanosuchus in its own family, Wanosuchidae, within the group Sebecosuchia.
Wanosuchus belongs to the parent group Eusuchia.
Wanosuchus is known from Paleocene-age rocks in southern Anhui, China.
Wanosuchus lived from 66 to 56 million years ago during the Danian to Thanetian stages.
